Market stance

Friday was a down day across the indexes — SPY −0.36%, QQQ −1.20% and IWM −0.32% — while the tape split between Venu's twelve strongest-looking names ripping higher and the NVDA aftermath dragging on, with NVDA itself printing a new 52-week low of 162.85 ahead of Tuesday's earnings.

Market — SPY · QQQ · IWM · TLT

Macro overlay — from their posts, not our data
Friday was a down day across the indexes — SPY −0.36% to 754.37, QQQ −1.20% to 679.89, IWM −0.32% to 277.54 and TLT −0.43% to 79.38 — and the day's real story was the split between the tape's two halves. The macro overlay is the FAA nationwide ground stop, the third time ever: Enrich posts “FAA ISSUES NATIONWIDE GROUND STOP”, Prof posts the notice itself (“All flight departures have been halted”, until 2200 UTC), and Remz adds “FAA HAS NOT GIVEN ANY INDICATION WHEN GROUNDSTOP MIGHT BE LIFTED” — and Enrich ties it straight to a name, “I see why $CRWD is up 95% YTD. Cybersecurity first with $MSFT, now all airlines in the US.” The second overlay is the Microsoft outage: Prof lists it in his “just this week” recap (“Nvidia CEO resigns, US goes through groundstop, Microsoft get a global outage, Drone attack — Dud what the hell?”) and iain dates it precisely (“Major Microsoft outage hits Outlook, Teams + Copilot across dozens of countries (Nov 12-13)”). iain supplies the market stance for the window — “the market has officially achieved equal opportunity destruction. perma-bulls? COOKED. dip buyers? DEEP FRIED. perma-bears overstaying shorts? AIR FRIED. And me?? sitting in cash doing absolutely nothing onna beach” — and his week-in-review frames the month (“4 different historical eras this month alone”: Big Tech/AI earnings disappointments, the Jensen Huang resignation, the midterm elections, Middle East/Iran-related oil). Sean supplies the trader's week: “+$29k for the week. Overextension reversals early in the week then got short into the key EMA's. Being patient. Super picky. Waiting for my spots.” — and his patience posts bookend it (“If you want to make money in trading you must master the art of waiting”, “Getting rich in the markets is alot more boring than people think”). The NVDA aftermath is the other half of the tape: NVDA fell another 2.01% to a new 52-week low of 162.85 on 1.85x volume, 18.22% under its 50-week EMA — and Prof supplies the next test, “Now Nvidia Earnings next week”, with his Earnings Whispers calendar putting NVDA on Tuesday after close. The money, meanwhile, is in Venu's list: twelve strongest-looking names, and Friday's tape agreed — U +5.24% to a new 52-week high with three traders on it (Sean's 4x-volume gap holding, Enrich's flag with “room to $55”, Venu's list), SPOT +2.36% back over the 609.88 base top it lost Thursday (Sean's tight flag off the 8 EMA, Venu's base), DUOL +5.01% to a new 3-month high, CROX +4.36% and PCOR +0.50% to new 52-week highs, FROG +2.71% to a new high on Sean's 35% gap, APP +3.92% holding near the highs after its 30%+ gap, FISV +3.71% into its range top, TOST +3.46% with the cup-and-handle forming, YOU and TMDX and CLX all on the list again. Enrich's other call is the long one: “Peter Beck is a generational talent leading a generational company. $RKLB to $200” — but RKLB closed −3.96% at 61.53, 59.04% under its high and below every average, so the framework treats the $200 as a long-term call, not a trigger. Your process gives three genuine qualifiers with triggers above the close: U (three traders, base breakout, trigger $55), SPOT (flag breakout reclaimed, trigger 627.66) and FROG (35% gap holding at new highs) — plus CROX, PCOR and DUOL as new-high holds and APP as a repair in progress (trigger 410.00). The declines, not entries: NVDA at a new 52-week low into Tuesday's earnings, GOOGL 26.54% under its high, RKLB in decline. The extended names: AAPL printed a new 52-week high at 356.27 with no pullback, U is 21.65% above its 50-day EMA, and CRWD is up 95% YTD per Enrich with no setup. The discipline is in the framing: the indexes gave back ground and QQQ is the weakest of the four, but the strongest-looking names are breaking out — and Tuesday's NVDA print is the next test.

  • Level strength: Strong = 2+ confluent anchors (52w high/low, 3m swing, 50-day EMA, 30-week MA, 50-week EMA, trader-stated) within 0.75%, or a 52w extreme with 3+ weekly touches in the past year. Moderate = 1 anchor or 2–3 touches. Light = anything else. Touches count weeks whose high or low came within 0.75% of the level. Duplicate prices merge into one row carrying both labels. U's trigger 55.00 is Enrich's stated level; U's invalidation 48.43 is Enrich's chart level; SPOT's invalidation 609.88 is Sean's breakout line and Venu's base top; YOU's trigger 65.72 and TMDX's trigger 97.54 are Venu's chart levels; AAPL's, FROG's, CROX's and PCOR's triggers are their 52-week highs at the close; DUOL's, TOST's, FISV's and CLX's triggers are their 3-month swing highs.
